    The value of Global X is not just in the content, it's in the people in the room. You will be alongside New Zealand exporters at different stages of growth, from those entering new markets through to businesses scaling internationally. You will hear directly from economists, trade experts, and global market leaders, bringing perspectives from policy, practice, and real-world execution. You will connect with New Zealand Trade and Enterprise, industry partners, and international networks, offering insight into market access, support, and emerging opportunities. We know that for exporters, the right conversation can unlock as much value as the right insight. Make the most of your connections at Global X: https://lnkd.in/giM_HpEa In partnership with New Zealand Trade and Enterprise and ExportNZ, and thanks to our sponsors DHL, Port of Auckland and New Zealand Export Credit (NZEC).

    In a market where conditions are changing faster than most strategies can keep up, the advantage sits with those who have both clarity and practical direction. Global X Summit on 15 September brings those two together in one place. • A clear understanding of the global economic context shaping export decisions • Insight into how trade policy and geopolitics are affecting market access and opportunity • A real-time view of what is working in global markets today • Practical sessions focused on AI, marketing, and staying competitive • First-hand perspectives from exporters who are actively growing offshore Across a full-day, the Summit is designed to move from big-picture shifts through to applied learning and peer insight, reflecting the way exporters need to operate today. For businesses navigating both opportunity and uncertainty, it is a rare chance to step back, sense-check direction, and return with a clearer view of what to prioritise next. Explore the full programme and secure your place at Global X: https://lnkd.in/giM_HpEa In partnership with New Zealand Trade and Enterprise and ExportNZ, and thanks to our sponsors DHL, Port of Auckland and New Zealand Export Credit (NZEC).

    Rising fuel costs, natural gas supply challenges and weather-related disruptions mean building energy resilience is becoming increasingly important for exporters. Join our Energy Resilience webinar on Tuesday 4 August to explore practical ways to improve energy efficiency, strengthen business resilience and reduce exposure to energy cost volatility. You'll also hear how these actions can help support long-term growth and meet evolving expectations in international markets. Hear international perspectives from Becky Lloyd (NZTE Beachhead Advisor), alongside insights from Aimee McCammon (Pic’s Peanut Butter) and Richard Briggs (EECA), on taking practical action and building resilience for future growth. Register now: https://lnkd.in/dj9Ex8fR #NZExporters #EnergyResilience #EnergyEfficiency #BusinessResilience

    In Aotearoa New Zealand, the rising of Matariki marks the Māori New Year. Known by many names across cultures and oceans, this cluster of nine stars reminds us that while we look up from different places, we are connected through shared hopes and responsibilities. At NZTE, we support businesses to grow internationally by strengthening connections, building capability and helping navigate global markets. One example is Waikawa Fishing Company, a whānau-led business from the Marlborough Sounds. With NZTE support, businesses like Waikawa Fishing Company are exploring new markets while building on their sustainable practices, including fishing methods designed to reduce environmental impact. In the spirit of Matariki, we are proud to support Māori exporters on their international growth journey. Learn more about how NZTE supports Māori businesses: https://lnkd.in/gWg7M7wK #NZTE #MāoriBusiness #ExportGrowth #Matariki #SustainableSeafood

    New Zealand's aerospace story is becoming much broader than space alone. Last week we brought together companies working across launch, advanced aviation, precision manufacturing and digital trust, providing a snapshot of the innovation happening across New Zealand. A privilege to hear from Dawn Aerospace, Rocket Lab, Kea Aerospace, United Machinists and Kry10 and to see the interest from Japanese stakeholders in building deeper connections and commercial partnerships with New Zealand. Held alongside the SPACETIDE Foundation July programme, the wider event provided a valuable opportunity to connect New Zealand innovators with founders, investors, researchers and industry leaders helping shape the future of aerospace in Japan and beyond. A huge thank you to everyone who contributed, particularly JAXA: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency and our colleagues across New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs & Trade, Invest New Zealand and the New Zealand Embassy in Tokyo team. Events like this remind me that some of the most valuable outcomes don't happen on stage — they happen in the conversations, introductions and new connections that follow. It was exciting to see so many people exploring opportunities to strengthen the New Zealand–Japan aerospace relationship.     What does a billion-dollar export industry built largely by SMEs look like? New Zealand's game development sector is giving us the answer. 🎮💰 The industry continues to gain momentum, with GDSR recipient studios reporting NZ$829 million in revenue for 2025/26, up 17% year on year. At the same time, the number of games in development has grown from 170 to 194, signaling a strong pipeline for future growth. 📈 But perhaps the most remarkable statistic is that 98% of revenue comes from exports. It's a reminder that some of New Zealand's fastest-growing global businesses aren't moving products across borders. They're exporting intellectual property, creativity, and digital experiences to customers around the world. 🌎 Kim Skoretz Charles Haddrell

    New Zealand–India trade is moving at pace. Two-way trade has nearly doubled since 2022 – from $2.0 billion to $3.9 billion. India is now New Zealand’s 11th largest bilateral trading partner. The historic visit of Indian Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to New Zealand this weekend – the first by an Indian PM in 40 years – and the announcement of a new Strategic Partnership and ambition to double trade by 2030, build on that momentum. Read more here:https://lnkd.in/d85dMw5J NZTE was proud to support the visit, helping to bring together over 50 New Zealand and Indian business leaders to explore opportunities for partnership, investment and commercial growth. Once in force, the New Zealand–India Free Trade Agreement will open even more doors across a range of sectors where New Zealand businesses bring world-class capability. NZTE is helping more exporters prepare, connect and grow in India than ever before.
